note: Dated events for this scenario, drawn only from mechanics the engine already has. Dates are the year and the week of that year. Magnitudes follow docs/rules/CONTENT-PACING.md. Titles and summaries are fictional framing with no real company or person names.

events.title: The technology bubble bursts
events.summary: Share prices of internet and technology firms fall hard. Orders for equipment and software dry up across the region.

events.title: The economy slips into recession
events.summary: Factories cut shifts and households hold back. The central bank starts cutting rates to cushion the fall.

events.title: Lenders pull back after the bankruptcies
events.summary: A string of big bankruptcies leaves banks cautious. Credit costs more for everyone but the strongest borrowers.

events.title: Steel import tariffs begin
events.summary: The government puts tariffs on imported steel to protect mills. Foreign steel arrives in smaller amounts and domestic steel prices firm up.

events.title: A labour dispute shuts a lake port
events.summary: Dockworkers at a major lake port walk out over contracts. Ships wait while shippers look for other routes.

events.title: Growth returns
events.summary: Orders pick up and hiring restarts. The central bank stops cutting and begins to lean the other way.

events.title: A housing and building boom
events.summary: Cheap credit and rising home prices send builders into overdrive. Demand for construction jumps.

events.title: An export boom
events.summary: A weak currency and hungry overseas buyers lift orders for the region's factories and farms.

events.title: A credit crunch
events.summary: A string of lender failures freezes borrowing. Spreads jump, orders fall and the central bank cuts hard.
